findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @pagai/mcp
findings.detail: 'pagai__mcp' launches @pagai/mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@pagai/mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): update_client
findings.detail: The description of 'pagai__mcp.update_client' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: hardcoded_recipient. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: hardcoded_recipient, entropy, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Change a customer's details — 'el correo de Pedro ahora es pedro@nuevo.cl'. Only the fields you pass change. Get client_id from find_clients.

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
